idea.title: Style mixed-script values with semantics, not DOM position
idea.summary: A reusable Arabic carousel threshold layout had styled whichever bidi element appeared last. Replacing that positional CSS with explicit label and value markup kept technical values readable even when RTL/LTR ordering changes.

context.goal: Improve reusable phone-size comparison readability without changing the carousel content model.
context.situation: The active carousel uses a segmented takeaway layout for two latency thresholds, rather than the generic comparison template.
context.problem: The value emphasis depended on bdi:last-child, which is a structural assumption that can misidentify text when mixed RTL/LTR content changes.
context.investigation: Traced the active slide through its layout component and confirmed that the generic comparison CSS did not render this slide.
context.decision: Add semantic threshold label and value classes within the existing takeaway component and render each threshold as a restrained label/value row.
context.implementation: Replaced the positional selector with explicit semantic markup and shared segmented-layout CSS.
context.result: The current export shows Read P95 and Mutation P95 as readable labels with moderately emphasized values, and the renderer DOM reports two semantic value elements with no positional CSS selector.

learning_points: Mixed-script typography is a data-structure concern as well as a CSS concern.
A visually similar layout may use a different component than its apparent template category.
Semantic classes prevent bidi text order from changing the styling target.
story_points: The initial assumption was that comparison CSS controlled the threshold slide.
Tracing the rendering route identified the actual segmented takeaway layout.
possible_angles: Why bdi:last-child is fragile in Arabic technical UI.
The debugging value of tracing a layout ID to its real component.
How semantic markup protects typographic hierarchy in mixed-language content.

notes: This is raw source material only and records the verified renderer change.
